reasons: F01, F06, F07, F16, F17, F18: no material weakness, no disagreements with the accountants, no prior-period correction and no SEC, government or class-action matters disclosed in the current filing.
F03: no auditor ICFR attestation (not required), so internal controls get less outside assurance.
F05: auditor change within two years. On its own this is a moderate governance flag, though no disagreements were reported (F06).
F22, F24: major acquisition in the year, and business combination is a critical audit matter. Purchase-price allocation and the goodwill/intangibles judgments are an area of estimation risk.
F25: voluntary accounting change in the year, which can move reported results and weakens comparability.
F20, F26: incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS together with a non-GAAP emphasis gives management a motive to manage results.

R01, R11, R18, R04: DSRI of 1.57 and receivables growth 0.81 above sales growth (with SGI 1.41) mean receivables outpaced revenue. Part of this may come from the acquisition, but it is the main revenue-quality flag.
R03, R13: AQI of 1.17 and soft-assets share of 0.92 show a rising non-current/soft asset base, consistent with acquired intangibles and goodwill.

R08, R10, R19: large negative accruals (TATA -0.16, RSST -0.20) and operating cash flow at 6.95x net income argue against accrual-driven earnings inflation. The cash flow may be inflated by movements in customer-funds or restricted cash.
R09, R17: Beneish M-score of -2.30 is below the -1.78 threshold and Dechow F-score of 0.81 is below 1.0. Neither composite model flags likely manipulation.
R02, R06, R07, R14, R15, R16: gross margin, SG&A, leverage, cash sales and ROA show no unusual movement, and no securities were issued.
